metadata.description: The nested case. dist/packages/firebase-server is ONE npm package with 10 rollup entry points, not 10 packages: the nine children (firebase-server-mailgun, -model, -oidc, -twilio, -zoho, -calcom, -discord, -mcp, -test) compile INTO this directory and are named by this package's own dist `exports`. So this target is the sole deliverable and the sole owner of the directory, and the children deliberately have no `build` of their own -- there is nothing they could publish.  What changed: the sequential `npx nx run <child>:build-base` shell-outs became dependsOn EDGES. Each of those was a separate Nx process with its own task graph, so nothing deduped and `parallel: false` was the only ordering; now it is one process, one graph, and Nx schedules the children by their real production layering -- 3 waves (parent; -mailgun/-model/-oidc/-twilio; -zoho/-calcom/-discord/-mcp/-test) instead of 10 sequential steps. The old hand-written order was not even a valid topological sort: it built firebase-server-model third while the graph put firebase-server-test, which model appeared to depend on, tenth. The finalize stays this target's own command, so it runs after every entry point is built -- dependsOn does not order its own entries, which is exactly why the post-step must not be a sibling list item.  Outputs stay the whole directory, which is correct HERE precisely because this task is its only writer: the cache payload is always complete, so the restore that remove()s the directory always puts all of it back.

`^build`, NOT the `^build-base` @nx/rollup/plugin infers. @nx/js remaps @dereekb/* imports to the dist DIRECTORY, so TypeScript reads that directory's package.json `exports` to resolve them -- and rollup writes `.` as {import, types} until that dependency's own `build` reorders it. `^build-base` would compile this package against un-finalized dependencies.
